newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: New Star to counter Savoy's takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: New Star to counter Savoy's takeover bid.

text.p: South Korea's New Star Trading Co plans to offer a 1-for-100 bonus issue in early May as part of its efforts to deter a takeover bid by Savoy Hotel, a New Star executive said on Wednesday.
"We see Savoy's recent purchase of an additional stake in our company as a takeover bid," Kim Hong-gil, an executive director of New Star, told Reuters.
New Star will issue 4,775 new common shares and allocate them to shareholders registered as of May 2.

A Korea Stock Exchange statement said earlier on Wednesday that South Korea's Savoy Hotel had raised its stake in New Star to 24.7 percent from 13.59 percent by buying 11.11 percent of New Star's outstanding shares in the open market.
Savoy's increased stake outpaced the combined 23.17 percent stake held by the family of New Star's chairman, the current owner of the company.
It was not clear from the statement whether Savoy's purchase of the additional shares was aimed at taking over New Star.
Kim said the bonus issue will help the company's current owners increase their stake and allow them to review an exact list of shareholders.

Under South Korea's securities regulations, holders of less than 100 shares will be given cash instead of new shares, Kim said. The company will receive the bonus shares of the these small shareholders, he said.
New Star will also benefit from the bonus issue because the list of shareholders will be closed for 14 days from May 3, which will allow the company to analyse the shareholding structure, he said.
